name: orders out-of-order records and preserves equal-timestamp insertion order
input: four inserts including two records at timestamp three
test:
store = LogStore()
store.add(5, 'late')
store.add(3, 'first-three')
store.add(3, 'second-three')
store.add(1, 'early')
assert list(store.iter_range(1, 3)) == [(1, 'early'), (3, 'first-three'), (3, 'second-three')]
assert list(store.iter_range(4, 4)) == []

name: returns fresh lazy iterators for inclusive range queries
input: a five-record store queried by next and then from the beginning
test:
store = LogStore()
for timestamp in [10, 8, 9, 11, 12]:
    store.add(timestamp, str(timestamp))
rows = store.iter_range(9, 11)
assert not isinstance(rows, list)
assert next(rows) == (9, '9')
assert list(rows) == [(10, '10'), (11, '11')]
assert list(store.iter_range(9, 11)) == [(9, '9'), (10, '10'), (11, '11')]

name: validates log records and range boundaries
input: non-integer timestamps, non-string messages, and invalid intervals
test:
store = LogStore()
def must_raise(call):
    try:
        call()
    except ValueError:
        return
    raise AssertionError('expected ValueError')
must_raise(lambda: store.add(True, 'x'))
must_raise(lambda: store.add(1, 2))
must_raise(lambda: store.iter_range(3, 2))
must_raise(lambda: store.iter_range(1.5, 2))
must_raise(lambda: store.iter_range(1, False))
